edition.stripNote: Fri 27 Nov. A broad metals rally extended into Friday's shortened post-Thanksgiving session as short covering, a weaker dollar and improved risk appetite lifted commodities across the board. Silver surged 4.0% to $43.17 per ounce — its largest daily gain in three weeks — while copper jumped 4.1% to $5.60 per pound on the LME, recovering sharply from Wednesday's 11-month low. Gold rose 2.0% to $3,637, its second consecutive advance after a twelve-session losing streak. Platinum gained 2.6% to $1,325; palladium was flat at $874. LME zinc rose approximately 2.5% to $3,600 per tonne, extending the Nyrstar Budel closure rally; nickel gained approximately 2.4% to $16,100; tin added approximately 2.0% to $38,700. Brent crude's January contract settled at $95.44 per barrel — down 1.2% from Thursday's Houthi-driven spike to $96.57 but still up 3.1% on the week, its first weekly gain of November. WTI settled at $83.08. The January Brent contract expires Monday November 30; February sits at approximately $91.90, a $3.50 backwardation reflecting near-term supply anxiety. OPEC+ ministers meet Sunday November 29 — Reuters sources indicate the group has agreed in principle to keep Q1 2027 output targets unchanged, though Iraq continues to push for a higher production ceiling. In grains, the shortened session saw divergent moves: soybeans rallied 2.4% to 1,266 cents on strong export demand, while corn fell 2.0% to 447 cents and wheat declined 2.9% to 567 cents. ICE cocoa climbed to a three-week high near $5,100 per tonne on Ivory Coast supply concerns — 2026/27 port arrivals down 47% year on year. Lithium carbonate crashed 7.8% on the week to ¥84,350 per tonne, now below the cash cost of production from purchased spodumene at ¥84,601. Bitcoin held above $61,000 through a $7 billion Deribit options expiry, closing at approximately $61,500 (+1.8%); Ethereum rose 2.0% to $1,733. The Fear and Greed Index remains at 12, deep in extreme fear territory. Newcastle coal edged up to approximately $150, with the energy complex rally supportive. The December 9–10 FOMC meeting looms as the next major catalyst.

overview: A broad metals rally extended into Friday's shortened post-Thanksgiving session as short covering, a weaker dollar and improved risk appetite lifted commodities across the board. Silver surged 4.0% to $43.17 per ounce — its largest daily gain in three weeks — while copper jumped 4.1% to $5.60 per pound on the LME, recovering sharply from Wednesday's 11-month low. Gold rose 2.0% to $3,637, its second consecutive advance after a twelve-session losing streak that had pushed spot to a 15-month low. Platinum gained 2.6% to $1,325; palladium was flat at $874. LME zinc rose approximately 2.5% to $3,600 per tonne, extending the Nyrstar Budel closure rally; nickel gained approximately 2.4% to $16,100; tin added approximately 2.0% to $38,700. Brent crude's January contract settled at $95.44 per barrel — down 1.2% from Thursday's Houthi-driven spike but still up 3.1% on the week, its first weekly gain of November. WTI settled at $83.08. Bitcoin held above $61,000 through a $7 billion Deribit options expiry, closing at approximately $61,500. The Fear and Greed Index remains at 12.

OPEC+ ministers meet Sunday November 29 to decide Q1 2027 output policy — Reuters sources indicate the group has agreed in principle to keep targets unchanged, though Iraq continues to push for a higher production ceiling. The Brent January contract expires Monday, with the February rollover priced at approximately $91.90 — a $3.50 backwardation reflecting near-term supply anxiety. In grains, the shortened session saw divergent moves: soybeans rallied 2.4% to 1,266 cents on strong export demand, while corn fell 2.0% to 447 cents and wheat declined 2.9% to 567 cents. ICE cocoa climbed to a three-week high near $5,100 per tonne, driven by Ivory Coast 2026/27 port arrivals down 47% year on year and Ecuador rainfall damage. Lithium carbonate crashed 7.8% on the week to ¥84,350 per tonne — now below the cash cost of production from purchased spodumene — as Australian mine output continues to ramp. China's gallium, germanium and antimony export-control extension to January 27, 2027 has stabilised critical mineral prices, with the original November 27 deadline now passed without disruption. The December 9–10 FOMC meeting looms as the next major catalyst.

watchItems.title: OPEC+ meets Sunday November 29 to decide Q1 2027 output — sources say targets to hold, but Iraq pushes for higher ceiling
watchItems.text: OPEC+ ministers meet Sunday November 29 to decide first-quarter 2027 output policy. Reuters sources indicate the group has agreed in principle to keep production targets unchanged, but Iraq's oil minister Basim Mohammed Khudair said Friday that Baghdad is negotiating to raise its production ceiling. The timing is complicated: Brent at $95 on geopolitical risk (Houthi Jazan strike, Hormuz mine campaign) gives the group less incentive to add barrels, while producers pushing for higher quotas can point to supply tightness. The Brent January contract expires Monday November 30, and the $3.50 backwardation to February ($91.90) reflects near-term anxiety. Any surprise — a failure to agree, unexpected production increases, or an Iraq walkout — could move crude $5–10 in either direction. Goldman Sachs's December Brent forecast of $105 and $140 risk scenario remain operative.

watchItems.title: Bitcoin holds $61,500 through $7B options expiry as Arthur Hayes warns of weekend 'crypto dump'
watchItems.text: Bitcoin closed Friday at approximately $61,500 after navigating a volatile session that included a flash crash to $58,975 in the morning before recovering above $60,000. The $7 billion Deribit options expiry settled more than $10,000 below max pain, suggesting potential for continued volatility. Arthur Hayes warned of a weekend 'crypto dump' tied to post-expiry repositioning. November spot-ETF net outflows have reached a record $5.39 billion with BlackRock's IBIT carrying 85% of redemptions. The Fear and Greed Index sits at 12 — deep extreme fear. BTC is down approximately 20% month to date and 51% from its all-time high of $126,198. Key support at $58,000; resistance at $64,441.

watchItems.title: Lithium carbonate crashes below production cost — ¥84,350/t now below cash cost of ¥84,601 from purchased spodumene
watchItems.text: Battery-grade lithium carbonate closed at ¥84,350 per tonne on Friday — down 7.8% in a week and now below the cash cost of production from purchased spodumene at ¥84,601. Spodumene concentrate prices are falling in tandem: Brazilian CIF China dropped 8.3% to $1,105 per tonne, while SMM's Australian brand index plunged 10.5% to $1,060. Lithium carbonate is down 28.8% year to date. The decline is being driven by ramping Australian mine supply and additional capacity coming online outside China in Q4 2026. Goldman Sachs projects a 444,000-tonne global surplus by 2028. The key question is whether production curtailments follow now that prices have breached cash costs.

watchItems.title: Cocoa climbs to three-week high near $5,100 — Ivory Coast 2026/27 port arrivals down 47% year on year
watchItems.text: ICE cocoa climbed to a three-week high near $5,100 per tonne on Friday, driven by tightening supply fundamentals. Ivory Coast farmers delivered just 53,748 tonnes to ports in the week ended November 22 — versus 102,112 tonnes a year earlier — bringing 2026/27 cumulative arrivals to 330,843 tonnes, down 47% year on year. Ecuador rainfall damage (more than 10,000% above October norms) has further disrupted supply, while black pod disease continues spreading in West Africa. StoneX forecasts a 64,000-tonne deficit in the 2026/27 market. Against this, ICE warehouse inventories sit at a 2.5-year high of 3.89 million bags, and planned S&P GSCI rebalancing in early 2027 could reduce cocoa's index weighting.

desk.name: Gold
desk.m: COMEX Dec settle $3,639.60 · second consecutive advance after 12-session slide · dollar eased · short covering · largest weekly gain since Nov 6 · Dec hike ~98% · OPEC+ Sun
desk.sum: Gold rose 2.0% to approximately $3,637 per ounce on Friday, its second consecutive advance after a twelve-session losing streak that had pushed spot to a 15-month low on Wednesday. The COMEX December settlement was $3,639.60. The dollar eased during the shortened post-Thanksgiving session, and broad-based short covering lifted the entire precious metals complex. Gold posted its largest weekly gain since the week ending November 6. Rate-hike expectations for the December FOMC remain at approximately 98%. OPEC+ meets Sunday. Key support at $3,600; resistance at $3,700.

desk.name: Silver
desk.m: COMEX Dec settle $43.167 · largest daily gain in 3 weeks · gold-silver ratio narrowed to ~84 · short covering · largest weekly gain since Nov 6
desk.sum: Silver surged 4.0% to $43.17 per ounce on Friday — its largest daily gain in three weeks — as broad-based short covering and a weaker dollar lifted the entire precious metals complex. The COMEX December settlement was $43.167. The gold-silver ratio narrowed from approximately 86 to 84, reflecting silver's outperformance. Silver posted its largest weekly gain since the week ending November 6, alongside gold. The industrial metal component of silver demand amplified the move as copper and LME base metals also rallied sharply. Key support at $42; resistance at $45.

desk.name: Oil
desk.m: Jan settle $95.44 (-1.2%) · eased from Thu Houthi spike · first weekly gain of Nov (+3.1%) · Jan expires Mon Nov 30 · Feb ~$91.90 · WTI $83.08 · Goldman: $105 Dec, $140 risk · OPEC+ Sun Nov 29 · Iraq pushing higher ceiling
desk.sum: Brent crude's January contract settled at $95.44 per barrel on Friday — down 1.2% from Thursday's Houthi-driven $96.57 close but still up 3.1% on the week, its first weekly gain of November after a three-week losing streak. WTI settled at $83.08. The January contract expires Monday November 30, and the February rollover at approximately $91.90 carries a $3.50 backwardation reflecting near-term supply anxiety. OPEC+ meets Sunday with Reuters sources indicating Q1 2027 targets will hold, though Iraq is pushing for a higher ceiling. Iran's Hormuz campaign continues. Goldman Sachs's December forecast of $105 and $140 risk scenario remain operative.

desk.name: Copper
desk.m: LME ~$12,345/t · sharp rebound from Wed 11-month low · COMEX March rose as much as 6.3% intraday · short covering · still down ~12% in Nov
desk.sum: Copper jumped 4.1% to $5.60 per pound (approximately $12,345 per tonne LME) on Friday, extending Thursday's recovery from Wednesday's 11-month low. COMEX March copper rose as much as 6.3% to $5.76 intraday before settling closer to $5.60. The rally was driven by broad-based short covering and improved risk appetite as the dollar eased. Physical conditions remain tight, with record Yangshan premiums. Copper is still down approximately 12% in November. The recovery's durability will be tested next week. Key support at $5.38/lb ($11,860/t); resistance at $5.76/lb ($12,700/t).

desk.name: Coal
desk.m: Edged up from $145 · energy complex rally supportive · Brent $95 · LNG supply crisis intact · up ~40% YTD · OPEC+ Sun
desk.sum: Newcastle coal edged up to approximately $150 per tonne, supported by the broader energy complex rally. Brent crude's sustained elevation near $95 is supportive for coal-to-gas substitution economics. Coal is up approximately 40% year to date, driven almost entirely by the Hormuz gas shock and QatarEnergy's force majeure. The near-term outlook remains constructive given tight LNG supply, though the broader macro headwinds that have weighed on industrial commodities continue to cap sustained upside. OPEC+ meets Sunday.

desk.name: Platinum
desk.m: Spot ~$1,325 · second advance after Wed 15-month low · short covering · South African supply still constrained · dollar eased
desk.sum: Platinum rose 2.6% to approximately $1,325 per ounce on Friday, its second consecutive advance from Wednesday's 15-month low. The recovery was driven by broad-based precious metals short covering and a weaker dollar in the shortened session. South African mine supply remains constrained, and hydrogen electrolysis demand provides structural long-term support. Platinum posted gains alongside the broader metals complex. Key support at $1,290; resistance at $1,350.

desk.name: Palladium
desk.m: Flat at $874 · failed to participate in broader metals rally · still below $900 · EV transition headwind persists · thin trade
desk.sum: Palladium was essentially flat at approximately $874 per ounce on Friday, failing to participate meaningfully in the broad precious metals rally that lifted gold, silver and platinum. Palladium remains below $900, reflecting the structural headwind from the EV transition — fewer catalytic converters needed in battery-electric vehicles. Down approximately 38% year on year. The divergence from other precious metals underscores palladium's unique demand vulnerability. Key support at $843; resistance at $900.

desk.name: Hormuz Terminal
desk.m: Houthi Jazan refinery strike Thu · Houthi claimed Ras Tanura attack Wed · 266 vessels blacklisted · IRGC mine campaign ongoing · Brent $95 · 3 US carriers · OPEC+ Sun Nov 29
desk.sum: The Strait of Hormuz crisis continued Friday with the aftermath of Thursday's Houthi drone strike on Saudi Arabia's Jazan refinery — which killed a worker and temporarily halted some operations — and Wednesday's claimed Houthi attack on the Ras Tanura terminal. Iran's vessel blacklist stands at 266, aiming to deny salvage services to attacked ships. IMF PortWatch recorded just 1 transit on November 22, compared to a pre-crisis baseline of 85 per day. Brent eased to $95.44 from Thursday's spike but remains elevated. Three US carrier strike groups remain in the Gulf. OPEC+ meets Sunday.
desk.src: straits.live · Insurance Journal · gCaptain · UKMTO · JMIC · Reuters

desk.name: Corn
desk.m: Dec settle 446.75¢ · shortened post-Thanksgiving session · profit-taking after Wed's 1.3% gain · export demand intact · OPEC+ Sun
desk.sum: December corn settled at approximately 447 cents per bushel on Friday in a shortened post-Thanksgiving session, down 2.0% from Wednesday's close of 456 cents. The decline reflected profit-taking after Wednesday's 1.3% advance and the broader rotation out of grains into soybeans. Export demand fundamentals remain intact. Black Sea maritime disruption continues to support US export competitiveness. Markets return to normal hours Monday. Key support at 440 cents; resistance at 456 cents.

desk.name: Wheat
desk.m: Dec settle 566.5¢ · largest decline in a week · fund selling resumed · SovEcon: Russia exports 36Mt · shortened session
desk.sum: December SRW wheat settled at approximately 567 cents per bushel on Friday, down 2.9% from Wednesday's 584 cents in a shortened post-Thanksgiving session. Fund selling resumed after Wednesday's modest recovery. SovEcon's Russian wheat export estimate of 36 million tonnes — below the USDA forecast — continues to provide some structural support, but short-term technicals have turned bearish. The dollar eased slightly, a modest positive for export competitiveness. Key support at 560 cents; resistance at 584 cents.

desk.name: Soybean
desk.m: Jan settle 1,266.25¢ · demand bulls lifted prices in shortened session · export commitments up ~80% YoY · meal support intact · soybean fund rose 2.08% for 5th straight day
desk.sum: January soybeans rallied 2.4% to 1,266 cents per bushel on Friday, the standout performer in the grain complex during the shortened post-Thanksgiving session. The Teucrium Soybean Fund rose 2.08% for a fifth consecutive day. Strong export demand — US soybean export commitments remain up approximately 80% year on year — and soybean meal strength continue to provide structural support. The dollar's slight pullback was a modest tailwind for US export competitiveness. Key support at 1,236 cents; resistance at 1,280 cents.

desk.name: Cryptocurrencies
desk.m: ETH $1,733 +2.0% · $7B Deribit options expired · $5.39B record Nov ETF outflows · Hayes warns weekend dump · Fear & Greed 12 · down ~20% MTD
desk.sum: Bitcoin closed Friday at approximately $61,500, up 1.8%, after a volatile session that included a morning flash crash to $58,975 before recovering above $61,000. Ethereum rose 2.0% to $1,733. The $7 billion Deribit options expiry settled more than $10,000 below max pain. November spot-ETF outflows have reached a record $5.39 billion, with BlackRock's IBIT carrying 85% of redemptions. Arthur Hayes warned of a weekend 'crypto dump' tied to post-expiry repositioning. The Fear and Greed Index sits at 12 — deep extreme fear. BTC is down approximately 20% month to date. Key resistance at $64,441; support at $58,000.

desk.name: LNG
desk.m: JKM steady near $28 · TTF ~$28.5 · HH Jan settled $3.49 (-4.5%) on milder weather outlook · Brent eased to $95 · QatarEnergy FM continues · OPEC+ Sun
desk.sum: The Asian LNG spot JKM holds near $28 per MMBtu. Henry Hub's January contract settled at $3.49 per MMBtu, down 4.5% on a milder US weather outlook. TTF remains near $28.50. The Houthi attack on Saudi Arabia's Jazan refinery continues to underscore energy supply route vulnerability. QatarEnergy's force majeure extends through at least end-December 2026. Brent's pullback to $95 from Thursday's spike provides marginal relief for oil-linked LNG contract pricing. OPEC+ meets Sunday.
desk.src: S&P Global Platts · Global LNG Hub · Trading Economics

desk.name: Sulfur
desk.m: FOB Kuwait ~$765 · Hormuz mine campaign ongoing · 266 vessels blacklisted · Houthi Jazan strike · Brent $95 · OPEC+ Sun
desk.sum: Sulfur remains elevated at approximately $1,200 per tonne CFR Southeast Asia. The ongoing Hormuz mine campaign and Thursday's Houthi strike on Saudi Arabia's Jazan refinery maintain supply-side risk for Middle Eastern sulfur logistics. FOB Kuwait holds near $765 (KPC). Iran's vessel blacklist at 266 ships continues to constrain salvage and transit operations in the Gulf. Brent crude's easing to $95 from Thursday's $96.57 is marginal. OPEC+ meets Sunday.

desk.name: Potash
desk.m: BPC India $383 CFR · China benchmark ~$348 · grains mixed Fri · soy +2.4% supportive · Brent $95 · OPEC+ Sun
desk.sum: Muriate of potash (MOP) CFR Brazil holds at approximately $358 per tonne. BPC's India contract remains approximately $25 above China's 2026 benchmark at $383 per tonne CFR. Friday's shortened US grain session saw mixed results — soybeans +2.4% supportive for fertiliser demand signals, though corn -2.0% and wheat -2.9% provide partial offset. Belarus and Russia still account for about 40% of global supply despite Western sanctions. Brent eased to $95.

desk.name: Antimony
desk.m: China suspension extended to Jan 27, 2027 · original Nov 27 deadline now passed without disruption · Rotterdam $18,300–19,000/t · prices stabilised · underlying controls remain
desk.sum: Chinese antimony (#1 ingot) holds near ¥92,000 per tonne. The original November 27 export-control deadline has now passed without disruption following China's two-month extension to January 27, 2027. Overseas antimony sits at approximately $18,300–19,000 per tonne in Rotterdam. Benchmark Mineral Intelligence notes that volumes reaching US buyers have been small since the suspension, and the two-month extension is unlikely to change that materially. The underlying licensing regimes remain in force. China produces close to half of global mined antimony.

desk.name: Gallium & Germanium
desk.m: European delivered Ga fell 9% to $3,150/kg per Benchmark · China domestic Ga ~$460/kg · Ge $15,500/kg · Nov 27 deadline passed · extension to Jan 27, 2027 · volumes to US remain small
desk.sum: Gallium holds near $2,100 per kilogram outside China on a wholesale basis. European delivered gallium (per Benchmark Mineral Intelligence) fell 9% to $3,150 per kilogram from $3,450 two weeks earlier, as the export-control extension to January 27, 2027 reduces near-term supply anxiety. Germanium holds at $15,500 per kilogram. The original November 27 deadline has now passed without disruption. Benchmark notes that volumes reaching US buyers remain small. China produces approximately 99% of global primary low-purity gallium. Non-China primary supply is expected to rise from 10 tonnes in 2026 to over 200 tonnes by 2030.

desk.name: Vanadium
desk.m: Steady at $5.30 · upstream tightness · VRFB adoption timeline uncertain · China-Russia-SA control 90%+ · export-control deadline passed without disruption
desk.sum: Vanadium pentoxide (V₂O₅) holds at approximately $5.30 per pound in Europe, supported by persistent upstream tightness. The gallium, germanium and antimony export-control deadline of November 27 has now passed without disruption following China's two-month extension to January 27, 2027. The long-term bull case rests on vanadium redox flow batteries (VRFBs) for grid-scale energy storage, but adoption timing remains uncertain. China, Russia and South Africa control over 90% of supply.

desk.name: Cocoa
desk.m: Three-week high · Ivory Coast 2026/27 arrivals -47% YoY · Ecuador rainfall damage · black pod spreading · ICE stocks 3.89M bags 2.5-year high · StoneX: 64k t deficit
desk.sum: ICE cocoa climbed to a three-week high near $5,100 per tonne on Friday, driven by tightening supply fundamentals. Ivory Coast farmers delivered just 53,748 tonnes to ports in the week ended November 22, compared with 102,112 tonnes a year earlier — bringing 2026/27 cumulative arrivals to 330,843 tonnes, down 47% year on year. Ecuador rainfall damage and spreading black pod disease in West Africa further weigh on supply. StoneX forecasts a 64,000-tonne deficit in the 2026/27 season. ICE warehouse inventories at a 2.5-year high of 3.89 million bags provide a partial offset.

desk.name: Cobalt
desk.m: Slight upward trend per SMM · price centre edging higher · Rotterdam $16–17/lb · DRC logistics disruption ongoing · NMC-to-LFP shift structural headwind
desk.sum: Cobalt is estimated near $33,000 per tonne, with the domestic spot market showing a slight upward trend per SMM's weekly review — the price centre is edging higher though the fluctuation range remains limited. Rotterdam standard-grade cobalt metal sits at $16–17 per pound. The NMC-to-LFP battery chemistry shift continues to weigh on the structural demand outlook. The LME base metals rally on Friday has provided some positive sentiment spillover. The market remains in structural surplus.

desk.name: Lithium
desk.m: Crashed 7.8% in a week · now below cash cost of ¥84,601 from purchased spodumene · spodumene Brazil CIF $1,105/t (-8.3%) · Aus brands $1,060/t (-10.5%) · down 28.8% YTD · curtailments expected
desk.sum: Chinese battery-grade lithium carbonate crashed to ¥84,350 per tonne — down 7.8% in a week and now below the cash cost of production from purchased spodumene at ¥84,601. Spodumene concentrate prices are falling in tandem: Brazilian CIF China dropped 8.3% to $1,105 per tonne while SMM's Australian brand index plunged 10.5% to $1,060. Lithium carbonate is down 28.8% year to date. Australian mine output continues ramping and additional capacity outside China is coming online in Q4 2026. The breach below cash costs raises the prospect of near-term production curtailments.

desk.name: Rubber
desk.m: $2.55/kg · SE Asia supply tight · fungal blight ongoing · Brent $95 raises synthetic rubber costs · auto demand solid
desk.sum: Natural rubber (RSS3) trades near $2,550 per tonne ($2.55/kg), range-bound. Southeast Asian supply remains tight, with Thailand, Indonesia and Malaysia producing 70% of global latex and still affected by Pestalotiopsis fungal leaf blight. Brent crude's easing to $95 from $97 provides marginal relief for synthetic rubber production costs but the gap still tilts toward natural rubber. Auto-sector demand remains solid. OPEC+ meets Sunday to decide output policy.

desk.name: Uranium
desk.m: Spot $90.02 on Nov 20 per UraniumThisWeek · Cameco spot indicator $91.55 Oct 30 · term price approaching $99–100/lb record · 78 reactors under construction · KHNP 15.6M lb tender bids due Dec 28 · miners sliding despite price
desk.sum: Uranium spot holds near $91 per pound U₃O₈, with UraniumThisWeek reporting $90.02 on November 20 and Cameco's month-end indicator at $91.55. Long-term contract prices are approaching $99–100 per pound — near a nominal record (TradeTech's LT indicator hit $99 on October 31). KHNP has launched a major tender for approximately 15.6 million pounds over 2028–2037, with bids due December 28. The IAEA counts 78 reactors under construction worldwide. Despite spot holding above $90, uranium miners (URNM ETF) have continued sliding. Cameco cut 2026 production guidance to 19.5–20.5 million pounds.

desk.name: Rare Earths
desk.m: Pr-Nd prices on the rise per SMM · export-control deadline passed · rare earth controls pause runs to Jan 10, 2027 · downstream demand sluggish
desk.sum: Neodymium-praseodymium (NdPr) oxide holds at approximately $72 per kilogram domestically in China. SMM reports that Pr-Nd prices are on the rise, with suppliers holding firm and limiting price concessions. The gallium, germanium and antimony export-control deadline of November 27 has passed without disruption, and China's separate rare earth controls pause runs to January 10, 2027. Downstream magnetic material orders remain sluggish. The broader metals rally on Friday has not meaningfully lifted rare earth sentiment.

desk.name: Manganese
desk.m: South Africa 37% · Gabon 18% · miners holding firm · CIF China flat · LME metals rally may lift steel demand sentiment · ore sales rising per Fastmarkets
desk.sum: Manganese ore (44% Mn content) trades near $4.40 per dry metric tonne unit CIF China, flat. Miners continue holding a firm pricing stance. Fastmarkets reports that manganese ore sales at Chinese ports have picked up, with high-grade prices reversing recent losses while low-grade prices are sliding more slowly. South Africa supplies about 37% of global ore and Gabon 18%. Friday's broad LME base metals rally may provide a modest lift to steel demand sentiment.

desk.name: Nickel
desk.m: LME 3M ~$16,100 · continued rebound from Wed 1-year low · short covering · Indonesian RKAB uncertainty · global surplus continues · still down ~12% in Nov
desk.sum: LME nickel rose approximately 2.4% to an estimated $16,100 per tonne on Friday, continuing Thursday's recovery from oversold conditions near a one-year low. The rally was part of a broad LME base metals rebound driven by short covering and improved risk appetite. Indonesian RKAB mining quota uncertainty persists — potential tightening provides a floor while the global nickel surplus from Indonesian NPI and HPAL expansions caps upside. Nickel remains down approximately 12% in November. Key support at $15,700; resistance at $16,500.

desk.name: Tin
desk.m: LME 3M ~$38,700 · continued recovery from Wed's 7.2% plunge · short covering · Myanmar ban constraining supply · still near 1-year low
desk.sum: LME tin rose approximately 2.0% to an estimated $38,700 per tonne on Friday, continuing the recovery from Wednesday's dramatic 7.2% plunge to a one-year low. Short covering drove the second consecutive day of gains. Structural supply constraints from Myanmar's Wa State mining ban and Indonesian export licensing tightness persist. Tin remains near its lowest level in a year despite two days of recovery. The rebound's durability will be tested when full trading resumes next week. Key support at $37,900; resistance at $39,500.

desk.name: Zinc
desk.m: LME 3M ~$3,600 · extended Nyrstar Budel closure rally · 160,000 t/yr capacity removed · TCs deeply negative · structural deficit · still up ~15% YoY
desk.sum: LME zinc rose approximately 2.5% to an estimated $3,600 per tonne on Friday, extending Thursday's Nyrstar Budel smelter closure rally. Budel — Europe's second-largest zinc plant with approximately 160,000 tonnes of annual capacity — has permanently closed, intensifying the structural supply deficit signalled by deeply negative treatment charges. Zinc is still up approximately 15% year on year, outperforming the broader base metals complex. The smelter closure narrative has provided insulation from the macro headwinds that weighed on other metals through November. Key support at $3,500; resistance at $3,700.

desk.name: Tungsten
desk.m: Rotterdam APT $2,750 · China FOB $1,845 · Western ~3.5x China · export-control deadline passed · extension to Jan 27, 2027
desk.sum: European tungsten APT holds at $2,750 per mtu in Rotterdam, while Chinese FOB sits at $1,845 per mtu — Western prices remain roughly 3.5 times Chinese domestic levels. The original November 27 export-control deadline has now passed without disruption following China's two-month extension to January 27, 2027. The market continues to reflect the fragmentation created by China's export controls. The rolling extensions maintain the status quo while keeping strategic leverage intact.

desk.name: Helium
desk.m: Up ~360% YTD · Ras Laffan repair 3–5 years · Houthi Jazan strike and Ras Tanura claim · Hormuz mine campaign ongoing · 266 vessels blacklisted
desk.sum: Grade-A helium trades near $390 per thousand cubic feet, at critical levels. This week's Houthi drone strikes — Thursday's successful attack on Jazan refinery and Wednesday's claimed strike on Ras Tanura — add further geopolitical risk to energy supply routes that also carry helium. Iran's Hormuz mine campaign continues with 266 vessels blacklisted. QatarEnergy's Ras Laffan facility repairs remain estimated at 3–5 years. Helium is up approximately 360% year to date, driven almost entirely by Qatar supply disruptions.

desk.name: Phosphate
desk.m: OCP 30% global · DAP $560/t · sulfur cost surge pressuring economics · grains mixed Fri · soy +2.4% supportive
desk.sum: Phosphate rock trades near $120 per tonne FOB Morocco, with Morocco's OCP Group controlling about 30% of global trade. DAP prices sit near $560 per tonne CFR India. The sulfur price surge continues to pressure phosphate production economics. Friday's grain session was mixed — soybeans +2.4% supportive for fertiliser demand, though corn -2.0% and wheat -2.9% weigh. Brent crude's easing to $95 is marginal for the probability of Middle Eastern sulfur supply normalising. OPEC+ meets Sunday.

quiz: Silver surged 4.0% to $43.17 per ounce on Friday — its largest daily gain in three weeks — as broad-based short covering and a weaker dollar lifted the entire precious metals complex in the shortened post-Thanksgiving session.
Gold spot fell 1.5% on Friday to $3,513 per ounce, extending its losing streak to thirteen sessions as the dollar strengthened further and December rate-hike expectations firmed at 100%.

Gold actually rose 2.0% to approximately $3,637 per ounce on Friday — its second consecutive advance after a twelve-session losing streak. The dollar eased during the shortened session and short covering lifted precious metals.
Brent crude's January contract settled at $95.44 per barrel on Friday — down 1.2% from Thursday's Houthi-driven spike, but still up 3.1% on the week for its first weekly gain of November.
LME copper fell 3% on Friday to $5.20 per pound, sliding to a new 12-month low as the dollar surged and China's property sector data disappointed, while other base metals followed copper lower.

LME copper actually jumped 4.1% to $5.60 per pound on Friday, recovering sharply from Wednesday's 11-month low as broad-based short covering and improved risk appetite lifted the entire base metals complex.
Bitcoin held above $61,000 through a $7 billion Deribit options expiry on Friday, closing at approximately $61,500, with November spot-ETF outflows reaching a record $5.39 billion.
Lithium carbonate prices in China rose 5% on Friday to ¥91,500 per tonne as electric vehicle sales exceeded expectations and downstream battery makers restocked ahead of Q1 2027.

Battery-grade lithium carbonate actually crashed 7.8% in a week to ¥84,350 per tonne — now below the cash cost of production from purchased spodumene at ¥84,601. Prices are down 28.8% year to date as Australian mine output ramps.

January soybeans rallied 2.4% to 1,266 cents per bushel on Friday in a shortened post-Thanksgiving session, outperforming corn and wheat as strong export demand and soybean meal strength provided support.
ICE cocoa fell to a two-month low of $4,200 per tonne on Friday as improved weather conditions in West Africa boosted mid-crop expectations and ICE warehouse stocks reached record highs.

ICE cocoa actually climbed to a three-week high near $5,100 per tonne on Friday, driven by tightening supply fundamentals — Ivory Coast 2026/27 port arrivals are down 47% year on year and Ecuador rainfall damage further disrupted output.
